newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close higher, November future expires.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close higher, November future expires.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Friday in a market which declined into inactivity after being dominated initially by the expiry of the November future, with next week's market seen unchanged or slightly lower.

"The market died in the afternoon after the November future expired. Normal investors kept away with trading activity basically only involving dealers. Next week we could start slightly lower or at the the same level," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.11 point up at 128.81, while its December future fell 0.55 point to 128.75 with 445 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Novo Nordisk finished unchanged at 1000 crowns, two days after announcing 14 percent higher first nine-month 1996 pre-tax profits and following a CSFB recommendation to buy the paper up to 1166-1177 crowns.
Coloplast ended unchanged at 680 crowns after tumbling 30 crowns on Thursday on a lower than expected 1995/96 result.
Carlsberg in contrast finished four up at 380, Copenhagen Airports climbed eight crowns to 633, with leading banks mixed.
Dden Danske ended the week three crowns down at 431, while rival Unidanmark signed off unchanged at 279. Overall turnover for the day was 811 million crowns.
